title.zh: 卷437 列傳二百二十四 荣禄 王文韶 张之洞 瞿鸿禨
title.en: Volume 437 Biographies 224: Rong Lu, Wang Wenshao, Zhang Zhidong, Qu Hongji
title.raw: 卷437 列傳二百二十四 荣禄 王文韶 张之洞 瞿鸿禨

sentences.zh: 榮祿，字仲華，瓜爾佳氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: Rong Lu, courtesy name Zhonghua, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Lu, whose courtesy name was Zhonghua, belonged to the Guwalgiya clan and was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 祖喀什噶爾幫辦大臣塔斯哈，父總兵長壽，均見忠義傳。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tasgha, assistant commissioner at Kashgar, and his father Changshou, regional commander, are both recorded in the Biographies of Loyalty and Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tasgha, who had served as assistant commissioner at Kashgar, and his father Changshou, a regional commander, both have entries in the Biographies of Loyalty and Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 榮祿以廕生賞主事，隸工部，晉員外郎。

translations.literal: Rong Lu, through yinsheng privilege, was granted the post of secretary and attached to the Ministry of Works, then promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege as a yinsheng, Rong Lu received appointment as a secretary in the Ministry of Works and was later promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 出為直隸候補道。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as an expectant circuit intendant in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He was then posted as an expectant circuit intendant in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 同治初，設神機營，賞五品京堂，充翼長，兼專操大臣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tongzhi reign, when the Shenji Camp was established, he was granted the rank of fifth-rank capital official, served as wing commander, and concurrently held the post of drill commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tongzhi reign, when the Shenji Camp was founded, he was given fifth-rank capital status, appointed wing commander, and made concurrent drill commissioner.

sentences.zh: 再遷左翼總兵。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to be commander of the Left Wing.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted again to commander of the Left Wing.

sentences.zh: 用大學士文祥薦，改工部侍郎，調戶部，兼總管內務府大臣。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Grand Secretary Wen Xiang, he was transferred to vice minister of the Ministry of Works, then moved to the Ministry of Revenue, and concurrently made superintendent of the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: On Grand Secretary Wen Xiang's recommendation, he became vice minister of Works, was transferred to Revenue, and was also appointed superintendent of the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 穆宗崩，德宗嗣統。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong died, Emperor Dezong succeeded to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Muzong's death, Emperor Dezong ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 榮祿言於恭親王，乃請頒詔，俟嗣皇帝有子，承繼穆宗。

translations.literal: Rong Lu spoke to Prince Gong, and they then requested that an edict be issued stating that when the succeeding emperor had a son, that son would inherit Muzong's line.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Lu urged Prince Gong to seek an edict providing that when the new emperor should have a son, that son would carry on Emperor Muzong's succession.

sentences.zh: 其後始定以紹統者為嗣，

translations.literal: Only afterwards was it finally settled that the one who succeeded to the line would be adopted as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Only later was it finally decided that the heir by succession would be adopted into Muzong's line.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，兼步軍統領。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu, he was also concurrently appointed Metropolitan Infantry Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangxu, he was also made concurrent Metropolitan Infantry Commander.

sentences.zh: 遷左都御史，擢工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Censor-in-Chief and promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Left Censor-in-Chief and promoted to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 慈禧皇太后嘗欲自選宮監，榮祿奏非祖制，忤旨。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Cixi once wished to choose palace eunuchs herself; Rong Lu memorialized that this was not ancestral institution and offended her will.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Cixi once wanted to select palace eunuchs herself; Rong Lu submitted that this violated ancestral practice and thereby drew her displeasure.

sentences.zh: 會學士寶廷奏言滿大臣兼差多，乃解尚書及內務府差。

translations.literal: When Academician Bao Ting memorialized that Manchu grandees held too many concurrent posts, Rong Lu was relieved of his ministries and his post in the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: When Academician Bao Ting reported that Manchu ministers were holding too many concurrent appointments, Rong Lu was stripped of his ministry posts and his Imperial Household superintendency.

sentences.zh: 又以被劾納賄，降二級，旋開復，出為西安將軍。

translations.literal: He was again impeached for taking bribes, demoted two ranks, soon restored, and sent out as general at Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: After he was impeached for bribery, he was demoted two ranks, soon reinstated, and appointed general at Xi'an.

sentences.zh: 二十年，祝嘏留京，再授步軍統領。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, while remaining in the capital for birthday felicitations, he was again appointed Metropolitan Infantry Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Guangxu, he stayed in the capital for the birthday celebrations and was again appointed Metropolitan Infantry Commander.

sentences.zh: 日本構釁，恭親王、慶親王督辦軍務，榮祿參其事。

translations.literal: When Japan provoked hostilities, Princes Gong and Qing supervised military affairs, and Rong Lu took part in them.
translations.idiomatic: When Japan provoked war, Princes Gong and Qing were put in charge of military affairs, and Rong Lu assisted them.

sentences.zh: 和議成，疏薦溫處道袁世凱練新軍，是曰「新建陸軍」。

translations.literal: After peace was concluded, he memorialized recommending Yuan Shikai, intendant of Wenzhou circuit, to train a new army, called the "Newly Created Army."
translations.idiomatic: Once peace was made, he recommended in a memorial that Yuan Shikai, intendant of the Wenzhou circuit, train a new army—the force known as the "Newly Created Army."

sentences.zh: 授兵部尚書、協辦大學士。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of War and Associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of War and Associate Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 疏請益練新軍，而調甘肅提督董福祥軍入衛京師。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking to expand training of the new army and to transfer the army of Gansu provincial commander Dong Fuxiang to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In a memorial he asked to expand the new army's training and to bring Gansu provincial commander Dong Fuxiang's troops to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，晉大學士，命為直隸總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was promoted to Grand Secretary and ordered to be governor-general of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Guangxu he was promoted to Grand Secretary and appointed governor-general of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 是時上擢用主事康有為及知府譚嗣同等參預新政，議變法，斥舊臣，召直隸按察使袁世凱入覲，超授侍郎，統練兵。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor promoted and employed the secretary Kang Youwei and the prefect Tan Sitong and others to participate in the new policies, discussed reform, dismissed old ministers, summoned Zhili provincial surveillance commissioner Yuan Shikai for audience, granted him extraordinary promotion to vice minister, and put him in charge of troop training.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then promoting Kang Youwei, a secretary, and Tan Sitong, a prefect, among others to take part in the new policies; reform was debated, veteran ministers were pushed aside, and Yuan Shikai, Zhili surveillance commissioner, was summoned to court, given a leap promotion to vice minister, and placed in command of military training.

sentences.zh: 榮祿不自安，御史楊崇伊奏請太后再垂簾，於是太后复臨朝訓政，召榮祿為軍機大臣，以世凱代之，命查拿康有為，斬譚嗣同等六人於市，以上有疾，詔徵醫；

translations.literal: Rong Lu felt ill at ease; censor Yang Chongyi memorialized asking the empress dowager to resume the curtain again; thereupon the empress dowager again held court behind the curtain to instruct in government, summoned Rong Lu as Grand Councilor, replaced him with Yuan Shikai, ordered Kang Youwei seized, executed Tan Sitong and five others in the market, and because the emperor was ill, an edict summoned physicians;
translations.idiomatic: Uneasy at these developments, Rong Lu watched as Censor Yang Chongyi asked the empress dowager to resume regency behind the curtain; the empress dowager then took up government again, recalled Rong Lu as a Grand Councilor, put Yuan Shikai in his former post, ordered Kang Youwei arrested, and had Tan Sitong and five others executed in public; because the emperor was said to be ill, physicians were summoned by edict;

sentences.zh: 復命榮祿管兵部，仍節制北洋海陸各軍。

translations.literal: Rong Lu was again ordered to administer the Ministry of War and still to control all Beiyang land and sea forces.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Lu was again put in charge of the Ministry of War and retained overall command of Beiyang land and naval forces.

sentences.zh: 榮祿乃奏設武衛軍，以聶士成駐蘆臺為前軍，董福祥駐薊州為後軍，宋慶駐山海關為左軍，世凱駐小站為右軍，而自募萬人為中軍，駐南苑。

translations.literal: Rong Lu then memorialized to establish the Wuwei Army: Nie Shicheng stationed at Lutai as the Front Army, Dong Fuxiang at Jizhou as the Rear Army, Song Qing at Shanhaiguan as the Left Army, Yuan Shikai at Xiaozhan as the Right Army, while he himself recruited ten thousand men as the Central Army, stationed at the Southern Park.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Lu then proposed the Wuwei Army: Nie Shicheng at Lutai as the Front Army, Dong Fuxiang at Jizhou as the Rear Army, Song Qing at Shanhaiguan as the Left Army, Yuan Shikai at Xiaozhan as the Right Army, while he personally raised ten thousand men for the Central Army at the Southern Park.

sentences.zh: 時太后議廢帝，立端王載漪子溥俊為穆宗嗣，患外人為梗，用榮祿言，改稱「大阿哥」。

translations.literal: At that time the empress dowager discussed deposing the emperor and establishing Prince Duan's son Pujun as Muzong's heir; fearing foreign obstruction, on Rong Lu's advice the title was changed to "Great Elder Brother."
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager then considered deposing the emperor and naming Prince Duan's son Pujun as heir to Muzong's line; fearing foreign interference, she followed Rong Lu's counsel and styled the boy "Great Elder Brother" instead.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，拳匪亂作，載漪等稱其術，太后信之，欲倚以排外人。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the Boxer bandits rose in disorder; Zaiyi and others praised their arts; the empress dowager believed them and wished to rely on them to drive out foreigners.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year the Boxer uprising broke out; Prince Duan and others extolled their magic, the empress dowager trusted them, and hoped to use them to expel foreigners.

sentences.zh: 福祥率甘軍攻使館，月餘不下；

translations.literal: Fuxiang led the Gansu army to attack the legations, and for more than a month could not take them;
translations.idiomatic: Dong Fuxiang led the Gansu troops against the legations, yet after more than a month they still had not fallen;

sentences.zh: 榮祿不能阻，載漪等益橫，京師大亂，駢戮忠諫大臣。

translations.literal: Rong Lu could not stop them; Zaiyi and others grew more overbearing; the capital fell into great disorder, and loyal remonstrating ministers were executed in pairs.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Lu could not restrain them; Prince Duan's faction grew ever more arrogant; the capital descended into chaos, and loyal ministers who remonstrated were slaughtered in groups.

sentences.zh: 榮祿踉蹌入言，太后厲色斥之。

translations.literal: Rong Lu staggered in to speak; the empress dowager rebuked him with a stern countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Lu stumbled in to remonstrate, but the empress dowager sharply rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 聯軍入京，兩宮西幸，駐蹕太原。

translations.literal: The allied armies entered the capital; the two palaces fled west and halted at Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the allied armies entered Beijing, the court fled west and made its halt at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 榮祿請赴行在，不許，命為留京辦事大臣。

translations.literal: Rong Lu requested to go to the traveling court; permission was denied, and he was ordered to serve as minister remaining in the capital to handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Lu asked to join the traveling court but was refused and appointed minister left in Beijing to manage affairs.

sentences.zh: 已而詔詣西安，既至，寵禮有加，賞黃馬褂，賜雙眼花翎、紫韁。

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered him to proceed to Xi'an; when he arrived, favor and ceremony were increased; he was granted the yellow jacket, bestowed double-eyed peacock feathers and a purple bridle.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned to Xi'an, where he was received with heightened favor: the yellow jacket, double-eyed peacock feathers, and a purple bridle were all bestowed on him.

sentences.zh: 隨扈還京，加太子太保，轉文華殿大學士。

translations.literal: He followed in escort back to the capital, was given the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and transferred to Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the court back to Beijing, was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and became Grand Secretary of the Wenhua Hall.

sentences.zh: 二十九年卒，贈太傅，諡文忠，晉一等男爵。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he died; he was posthumously given Grand Tutor, honored with the posthumous title Wenzhong, and advanced to first-class baron.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-ninth year; the court posthumously made him Grand Tutor, gave him the posthumous title Wenzhong, and raised his rank to first-class baron.

sentences.zh: 榮祿久直內廷，得太后信仗。

translations.literal: Rong Lu long served directly in the inner court and gained the empress dowager's trust and reliance.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Lu had long served at the inner court and enjoyed the empress dowager's full trust.

sentences.zh: 眷顧之隆，一時無比。

translations.literal: The height of favor shown him was unmatched in his day.
translations.idiomatic: No one of his time was favored as highly.

sentences.zh: 事無鉅細，常待一言決焉。

translations.literal: In matters great or small, one often waited for a single word from him to decide them.
translations.idiomatic: On matters great and small, affairs often hung on his single word.

sentences.zh: 王文韶，字夔石，浙江仁和人。

translations.literal: Wang Wenshao, courtesy name Kuishi, was a native of Renhe in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wenshao, whose courtesy name was Kuishi, came from Renhe in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年進士，銓戶部主事。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the second year of Xianfeng, he was selected as a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Xianfeng and was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 累遷郎中，出為湖北安襄鄖荊道。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to director, then went out as intendant of the An-Xiang-Yun-Jing circuit in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to director and was then posted as intendant of the An-Xiang-Yun-Jing circuit in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 左宗棠、李鴻章皆薦其才。

translations.literal: Zuo Zongtang and Li Hongzhang both recommended his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Both Zuo Zongtang and Li Hongzhang commended his ability.

sentences.zh: 擢按察使，遷湖南布政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner and transferred to Hunan financial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner and then made Hunan financial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 同治十年，署巡撫。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tongzhi he served as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Tongzhi he served as acting governor of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 黔苗亂熾，桂東淪寇域。

translations.literal: The Miao rebellion in Guizhou blazed fiercely, and eastern Guangxi fell into rebel territory.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao rebellion in Guizhou raged, and eastern Guangxi was overrun by rebels.

sentences.zh: 文韶條上援黔、防境機宜，以兵事屬按察使席寶田，督其部將蘇元春、龔繼昌等進剿，斬首逆張秀眉烏鴉坡，黔境平。

translations.literal: Wenshao itemized and submitted plans for aiding Guizhou and defending the borders; he entrusted military affairs to surveillance commissioner Xi Baotian, supervised his subordinate generals Su Yuanchun, Gong Jichang, and others in advance and suppression, beheaded the chief rebel Zhang Xiuhui at Wuyapo, and Guizhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshao laid out in detail how to aid Guizhou and guard the frontier, put military affairs in the hands of Surveillance Commissioner Xi Baotian, and directed subordinates such as Su Yuanchun and Gong Jichang in the campaign; the rebel leader Zhang Xiuhui was beheaded at Wuyapo, and Guizhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 文韶繪苗疆要塞圖，上之朝。

translations.literal: Wenshao drew a map of Miao frontier strongholds and presented it to the court.
translations.idiomatic: He drew a map of Miao frontier fortifications and submitted it to the court.

sentences.zh: 十一年，除真。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was confirmed in the regular post.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year his acting appointment was made permanent.

sentences.zh: 寧遠莠民倡亂，耒陽硃鴻英复妄稱明裔構眾，先後檄道員陳寶箴討平之。

translations.literal: In Ningyuan worthless people stirred rebellion; in Leiyang Zhu Hongying again falsely claimed Ming descent and raised a crowd; Wenshao successively ordered circuit intendant Chen Baozhen to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Ruffians in Ningyuan rose in revolt, and in Leiyang Zhu Hongying again falsely claimed descent from the Ming and gathered followers; Wenshao successively ordered Circuit Intendant Chen Baozhen to put down both outbreaks.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，遣總兵謝晉鈞平新化、衡、永土寇。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he dispatched regional commander Xie Jinjun to pacify native bandits in Xinhua, Hengzhou, and Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangxu he sent Regional Commander Xie Jinjun to suppress native bandits in Xinhua, Hengzhou, and Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 撫湘六年，內治稱靜謐焉。

translations.literal: In six years governing Hunan, internal administration was said to be tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: During six years as Hunan governor, his civil administration was regarded as notably calm.

sentences.zh: 入權兵部侍郎，直軍機。

translations.literal: He entered the capital to serve as acting vice minister of War and attend the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as acting vice minister of War and join the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 會歲旱，各省籥災，中旨罪己。

translations.literal: There happened to be drought that year; provinces reported disasters; an imperial rescript confessed fault.
translations.idiomatic: When drought struck and provinces reported disasters, the throne issued a self-reproaching edict.

sentences.zh: 文韶亦自陳無狀，詔革職留任。

translations.literal: Wenshao also confessed his own unworthiness; an edict stripped his rank but kept him in office.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshao likewise confessed his failures; he was ordered stripped of rank but kept at his post.

sentences.zh: 旋除禮部侍郎，兼總理衙門行走。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed vice minister of Rites and concurrently served in the Zongli Yamen.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice minister of Rites and given concurrent duty in the Zongli Yamen.

sentences.zh: 八年，御史洪良品、鄧承修劾雲南軍需案，文韶坐失察，奪二級。

translations.literal: In the eighth year censors Hong Liangpin and Deng Chengxiu impeached in the Yunnan military supplies case; Wenshao was punished for failure of supervision and deprived of two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Censors Hong Liangpin and Deng Chengxiu impeached officials in the Yunnan military supplies scandal; Wenshao was held negligent and stripped of two ranks.

sentences.zh: 乞養歸，終母喪，還前除。

translations.literal: He requested leave to nurse his parents and returned home; after completing mourning for his mother, he was restored to his former appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire and care for his parents, completed mourning for his mother, and was then restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed governor-general of Yunnan-Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was appointed governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 武定會匪陷富民、祿勸，人心恟懼。

translations.literal: The secret-society rebels of Wuding seized Fumin and Luquan; popular hearts were alarmed and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Secret-society rebels in Wuding took Fumin and Luquan, throwing the populace into panic.

sentences.zh: 文韶斬獲叛將，三日而定。

translations.literal: Wenshao beheaded and captured the rebel generals; within three days it was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshao captured and executed the rebel leaders, and order was restored within three days.

sentences.zh: 無何，鎮邊夷亂起，檄迤南道劉春霖分道進攻，拓地三百里。

translations.literal: Before long, disturbances among the frontier Yi arose; he ordered Yinan circuit intendant Liu Chunlin to attack by separate routes and extended territory three hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward frontier Yi tribes rose in revolt; he ordered Yinan Circuit Intendant Liu Chunlin to advance on several routes and extended control over three hundred li of territory.

sentences.zh: 徙建廳城於猛朗，募勇屯墾。

translations.literal: He moved and rebuilt the subprefectural city at Menglang and recruited braves for garrison colonization.
translations.idiomatic: He relocated the subprefectural seat to Menglang and recruited militia for garrison farming.

sentences.zh: 改臨安猛丁歸流，移府經歷駐其地。

translations.literal: He changed Mengding in Lin'an from native to regular administration and moved a prefectural assistant to be stationed there.
translations.idiomatic: He brought Mengding in Lin'an under regular administration and posted a prefectural assistant there.

sentences.zh: 其餘寇亂及土族叛服不常，皆隨時殄滅。

translations.literal: As for other bandit disorders and tribal groups whose submission and rebellion were inconstant, all were extinguished as occasion arose.
translations.idiomatic: Other outbreaks and restive native groups were suppressed whenever they appeared.

sentences.zh: 初，英、法並緬、越後，西南緣邊防務益棘。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Britain and France had annexed Burma and Vietnam, frontier defense along the southwest grew ever more difficult.
translations.idiomatic: After Britain and France had absorbed Burma and Vietnam, defense along the southwestern frontier grew increasingly difficult.

sentences.zh: 文韶綏靖各路土司，令自為守。

translations.literal: Wenshao pacified the various native chieftains and ordered them to guard themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshao pacified the native chieftains along the routes and ordered them to defend their own domains.

sentences.zh: 會日韓啟釁，詔入都詢方略。

translations.literal: When Japan and Korea provoked hostilities, an edict summoned him to the capital to consult on strategy.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out between Japan and Korea, he was summoned to the capital to advise on strategy.

sentences.zh: 既至，奉幫辦北洋之命。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he received orders to assist in managing Beiyang affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he was ordered to assist in Beiyang affairs.

sentences.zh: 鴻章赴日議和，文韶權直隸總督、北洋大臣。

translations.literal: When Hongzhang went to Japan to negotiate peace, Wenshao acted as governor-general of Zhili and Beiyang commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: While Li Hongzhang went to Japan to negotiate peace, Wenshao served as acting governor-general of Zhili and Beiyang commissioner.

sentences.zh: 和議成，實授。

translations.literal: When peace was concluded, he received the regular appointment.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was concluded, he received the appointment in full.

sentences.zh: 時關內外主客軍四百餘營，酌留湘、淮、豫三十營，餘悉散遣，士卒帖然。

translations.literal: At that time there were more than four hundred camps of regular and guest armies inside and outside the passes; he judiciously retained thirty camps of Xiang, Huai, and Yu troops and dispersed the rest; the soldiers were compliant.
translations.idiomatic: More than four hundred camps of regular and auxiliary troops then lay inside and outside the passes; he kept thirty Xiang, Huai, and Yu camps and discharged the rest, and the men accepted the arrangement peacefully.

sentences.zh: 建議籌修旅大砲台，謂：「旅順舊台密於防前，疏於防後，敵自大連灣入，遂失所芘；

translations.literal: He proposed planning repairs to the Lüda forts, saying: "The old forts at Lüshun were dense in defense to the front and sparse to the rear; when the enemy entered from Dalian Bay, protection was lost;
translations.idiomatic: He proposed rebuilding the Lüda fortifications, arguing: "The old forts at Lüshun were strong facing the sea but weak to the rear; when the enemy came in through Dalian Bay, they lost their cover;

sentences.zh: 大連舊台，專顧防海，未及防陸，敵自金州登岸，遂不能支。

translations.literal: the old forts at Dalian looked only to sea defense and did not reach to land defense; when the enemy landed from Jinzhou, they could not hold.
translations.idiomatic: the old forts at Dalian guarded only the sea and not the land; when the enemy landed from Jinzhou, they could not stand.

sentences.zh: 今重整海防，必彌其罅隙。」

translations.literal: Now in reorganizing coastal defense, the gaps must be closed.
translations.idiomatic: In rebuilding coastal defenses now, we must close every gap."

sentences.zh: 又請加意水師、武備各學堂，以儲將才，嫺武幹，俟財力稍足，徐圖擴充。

translations.literal: He also asked that the naval and military academies receive added attention to store up command talent and train martial ability, and that when finances were somewhat sufficient, expansion be pursued gradually.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged greater attention to the naval and military academies to cultivate commanders and martial skill, with gradual expansion once finances allowed.

sentences.zh: 又陳河運漕糧積弊，請蘇漕統歸海運，他若勘吉林三姓金礦、磁州煤礦，踵鴻章後次第成之，而京漢鐵路亦興築於是時矣。

translations.literal: He also stated the accumulated abuses of grain transport by the Grand Canal and asked that Jiangsu tribute grain be wholly shifted to sea transport; as for surveying the gold mines of the Three Surnames in Jilin and the coal mines of Cizhou, following Hongzhang they were completed in turn, and the Beijing-Hankou Railway was also begun at this time.
translations.idiomatic: He also described the abuses of canal grain transport and asked that Jiangsu tribute grain be sent entirely by sea; surveys of the Three Surnames gold mines in Jilin and the Cizhou coal mines, following Li Hongzhang's lead, were carried through in turn, and the Beijing-Hankou Railway was begun in this period as well.

sentences.zh: 又奏設北洋大學堂、鐵路學堂、育才館、俄文館，造就甚眾。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to establish Beiyang University, the Railway Academy, the Talent-Nurturing Hall, and the Russian Language School; very many were trained.
translations.idiomatic: He also founded Beiyang University, a railway school, the Talent-Nurturing Hall, and a Russian language school, training a great many students.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，入贊軍機，以戶部尚書協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he entered to assist the Grand Council as Minister of Revenue and Associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he joined the Grand Council as Minister of Revenue and Associate Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，拳匪仇教，文韶力言外釁不可啟，不見納。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the Boxers hated Christianity; Wenshao strongly urged that foreign trouble must not be provoked, but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, when the Boxers turned against Christianity, Wenshao strongly warned against provoking foreign powers, but his counsel was ignored.

sentences.zh: 宮車既出，三日，始追及懷來。

translations.literal: After the imperial carriage had departed, only after three days did he catch up at Huailai.
translations.idiomatic: The court had already fled west; three days passed before he caught up at Huailai.

sentences.zh: 自聯軍犯京，事急，兩宮召軍機，惟文韶一人入見，諭必侍行。

translations.literal: From the time the allied armies attacked the capital, when affairs were urgent, the two palaces summoned the Grand Council; only Wenshao alone was admitted to audience and instructed that he must attend in travel.
translations.idiomatic: When the allied armies threatened Beijing and the situation grew desperate, the court summoned the Grand Council but admitted only Wenshao, instructing him that he must accompany the flight.

sentences.zh: 至是立召對，泣慰之，遂隨扈，自晉入秦，晉體仁閣大學士。

translations.literal: At this he was immediately summoned for audience; weeping, they comforted him, and he then followed in escort; from Shanxi they entered Shaanxi, and he was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Tiren Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was then summoned at once; the empresses wept as they comforted him, and he joined the flight west from Shanxi into Shaanxi, being promoted to Grand Secretary of the Tiren Hall.

sentences.zh: 明年，改外務部會辦大臣，旋賞黃馬褂。

translations.literal: The next year he was changed to co-managing minister of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and soon granted the yellow jacket.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became co-managing minister of Foreign Affairs and was soon granted the yellow jacket.

sentences.zh: 署全權大臣，命先還京，佐辦中俄條約。

translations.literal: He served as plenipotentiary commissioner and was ordered to return to the capital first to assist in the Sino-Russian treaty.
translations.idiomatic: As acting plenipotentiary he was ordered back to Beijing ahead of the court to help negotiate the Sino-Russian treaty.

sentences.zh: 交還東三省及關外鐵路，事寧，賞雙眼花翎。

translations.literal: When the three eastern provinces and the railways outside the passes were returned and affairs were settled, he was granted double-eyed peacock feathers.
translations.idiomatic: After the three eastern provinces and the railways beyond the passes were restored and affairs settled, he received double-eyed peacock feathers.

sentences.zh: 充政務處大臣，督辦路礦總局。

translations.literal: He served as minister of the Bureau of Government Affairs and supervised the General Bureau of Railways and Mines.
translations.idiomatic: He served on the Bureau of Government Affairs and supervised the General Bureau of Railways and Mines.

sentences.zh: 轉文淵閣，晉武英殿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Wenyuan Pavilion and promoted to the Wuying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He moved from the Wenyuan Pavilion to Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，免直軍機。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year he was relieved of attendance at the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he left the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 明年，稱疾乞休。

translations.literal: The next year he pleaded illness and asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he cited illness and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 文韶歷官中外，詳練吏職，究識大體，然更事久，明於趨避，亦往往被口語。

translations.literal: Wenshao served in office inside and outside the capital, was well versed in official duties and understood the larger pattern, yet having long experience in affairs, he was clear about advancing and avoiding, and was also often subject to gossip.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshao served at court and in the provinces, knew official routine thoroughly, and grasped the larger picture; yet long experience had taught him how to advance and withdraw, and he was often criticized for it.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，鄉舉重逢，賜太子太保。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he again encountered the year of his provincial examination and was granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year he celebrated the anniversary of his provincial examination and was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 其冬，卒，年七十九，晉贈太保，諡文勤。

translations.literal: That winter he died, aged seventy-nine; he was posthumously advanced to Grand Tutor and honored with the posthumous title Wenqin.
translations.idiomatic: He died that winter at seventy-nine; the court posthumously made him Grand Tutor and gave him the posthumous title Wenqin.

sentences.zh: 張之洞，字香濤，直隸南皮人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhidong, courtesy name Xiangtao, was a native of Nanpi in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhidong, whose courtesy name was Xiangtao, came from Nanpi in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 少有大略，務博覽為詞章，記誦絕人。

translations.literal: In youth he had great strategic vision, devoted himself to wide reading and literary composition, and his memory was unmatched among men.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a youth he showed great vision, read widely, cultivated literary skill, and possessed a memory few could match.

sentences.zh: 年十六，舉鄉試第一。

translations.literal: At age sixteen he placed first in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he took first place in the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，成進士，廷對策不循常式，用一甲三名授編修。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi he became a jinshi; in the palace examination his policy essay did not follow the usual form, yet he was placed among the top three of the first class and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Tongzhi; his palace examination essay broke with convention, yet he still ranked among the top three of the first class and was appointed a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 六年，充浙江鄉試副考官，旋督湖北學政。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he served as associate examiner for the Zhejiang provincial examination, then was made educational commissioner of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he served as associate examiner for the Zhejiang provincial examinations, then was appointed educational commissioner of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 十二年，典試四川，就授學政。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he presided over the Sichuan examination and was thereupon appointed educational commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he served as chief examiner in Sichuan and was appointed educational commissioner there on the spot.

sentences.zh: 所取士多俊才，遊其門者，皆私自喜得為學塗徑。

translations.literal: Those he selected were mostly brilliant talents; those who studied under him all privately rejoiced that they had found a path in learning.
translations.idiomatic: Most of those he selected were outstanding scholars, and students who passed through his school privately rejoiced that they had found a true path in learning.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，擢司業，再遷洗馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangxu he was promoted to vice director of studies and again transferred to groom of the heir apparent's stud.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangxu reign he was promoted to vice director of studies and soon moved up to groom in the heir apparent's stud.

sentences.zh: 之洞以文儒致清要，遇事敢為大言。

translations.literal: Zhidong, as a literary scholar, attained a pure and exalted post, and in affairs dared to speak boldly.
translations.idiomatic: As a literary scholar he had risen to a prestigious court post and was not afraid to speak out boldly on public affairs.

sentences.zh: 俄人議歸伊犁，與使俄大臣崇厚訂新約十八條。

translations.literal: The Russians discussed returning Yili, and Minister to Russia Chonghou concluded a new treaty of eighteen articles.
translations.idiomatic: When Russia proposed returning Yili, Minister to Russia Chonghou negotiated a new treaty of eighteen articles.

sentences.zh: 之洞論奏其失，請斬崇厚，毀俄約。

translations.literal: Zhidong argued and memorialized its errors, asking that Chonghou be executed and the Russian treaty destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidong memorialized on its defects, demanding Chonghou's execution and the abrogation of the Russian treaty.

sentences.zh: 疏上，乃褫崇厚職治罪，以侍郎曾紀澤為使俄大臣，議改約。

translations.literal: When the memorial went up, Chonghou was stripped of office and punished; Vice Minister Zeng Jize was made minister to Russia to negotiate revision of the treaty.
translations.idiomatic: Once the memorial reached the throne, Chonghou was dismissed and punished, and Vice Minister Zeng Jize was sent to Russia to renegotiate the treaty.

sentences.zh: 六年，授侍講，再遷庶子。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed expositor, then again transferred to tutor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he became an expositor and was soon promoted to tutor in the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 复論紀澤定約執成見，但論界務，不爭商務，並附陳設防、練兵之策。

translations.literal: He again argued that in concluding the treaty Jize clung to fixed views, discussing only boundary affairs and not contending over commercial matters, and appended statements on defense and troop training.
translations.idiomatic: He again criticized Jize for clinging to preconceptions in the treaty talks, attending only to boundaries and not commercial rights, and appended proposals for frontier defense and military training.

sentences.zh: 疏凡七八上。

translations.literal: Memorials of this sort totaled seven or eight submissions.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted seven or eight such memorials in all.

sentences.zh: 往者詞臣率雍容養望，自之洞喜言事，同時寶廷、陳寶琛、張佩綸輩崛起，糾彈時政，號為清流。

translations.literal: Formerly literary officials generally cultivated reputation with easy grace; from the time Zhidong delighted in speaking on affairs, contemporaries Bao Ting, Chen Baochen, Zhang Peilun, and others rose, impeaching current policy, and were called the Pure Stream.
translations.idiomatic: Court literati had long cultivated reputation in comfortable ease; once Zhidong took to remonstrance, Bao Ting, Chen Baochen, Zhang Peilun, and others rose with him to criticize policy and were known as the Pure Stream faction.

sentences.zh: 七年，由侍講學士擢閣學。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted from expositor of the Hanlin Academy to academy bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was promoted from Hanlin expositor to academy bachelor.

sentences.zh: 俄授山西巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed governor of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed governor of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 當大祲後，首劾布政使葆亨、冀寧道王定安等黷貨，舉廉明吏五人，條上治晉要務，未及行，移督兩廣。

translations.literal: After a great famine, he first impeached financial commissioner Bao Heng, Jining circuit intendant Wang Ding'an, and others for corruption, recommended five upright officials, itemized essentials for governing Shanxi, but before they could be carried out he was transferred to govern Guangdong and Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: After a severe famine he impeached Financial Commissioner Bao Heng, Jining Circuit Intendant Wang Ding'an, and others for corruption, recommended five upright officials, and laid out essentials for governing Shanxi; before these measures could be enacted he was transferred to the two Guang provinces.

sentences.zh: 八年，法越事起，建議當速遣師赴援，示以戰意，乃可居間調解。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Franco-Vietnamese affair arose; he proposed that troops should quickly be sent to aid, showing a will to fight, and only then could one mediate between the parties.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when the Franco-Vietnamese conflict broke out, he urged that troops be sent at once to show a readiness to fight, arguing that only then could China mediate effectively.

sentences.zh: 因薦唐炯、徐延旭、張曜材任將帥。

translations.literal: He therefore recommended Tang Jiong, Xu Yanxu, and Zhang Yao as men fit to command armies.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Tang Jiong, Xu Yanxu, and Zhang Yao as capable commanders.

sentences.zh: 十年春，入覲。

translations.literal: In the spring of the tenth year he entered the capital for audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the tenth year he was summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 四月，兩廣總督張樹聲解任專治軍，遂以之洞代。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Governor-General Zhang Shusheng was relieved to devote himself solely to military affairs, and Zhidong replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Governor-General Zhang Shusheng was relieved of civil duties to concentrate on the war, and Zhidong took his place.

sentences.zh: 當是時，雲貴總督岑毓英、廣西巡撫潘鼎新皆出督師，尚書彭玉麟治兵廣東。

translations.literal: At that time Governor-General Cen Yuying of Yunnan-Guizhou and Governor Pan Dingxin of Guangxi both went out to command armies, and Minister Peng Yulin directed troops in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Cen Yuying, governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou, and Pan Dingxin, governor of Guangxi, were both in the field, while Minister Peng Yulin directed forces in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 越將劉永福者，故中國人，素驍勇，與法抗。

translations.literal: The Vietnamese general Liu Yongfu was formerly a Chinese, by nature fierce and brave, and resisted the French.
translations.idiomatic: The Vietnamese commander Liu Yongfu was originally Chinese, renowned for valor, and fought the French.

sentences.zh: 法攻越未能下，復分兵攻台灣，其後遂據基隆。

translations.literal: France attacked Vietnam but could not subdue it, then divided forces to attack Taiwan, and afterward seized Keelung.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to conquer Vietnam, France sent troops against Taiwan and soon seized Keelung.

sentences.zh: 朝議和戰久不決，之洞至，言戰事氣自倍，以玉麟夙著威望，虛己聽從之。

translations.literal: Court debate on peace or war long remained unsettled; when Zhidong arrived, talk of war doubled in spirit; because Yulin had long enjoyed great prestige, he humbled himself and followed his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The court long wavered between peace and war; Zhidong's arrival redoubled the war party's confidence, and he deferred to the long-respected Peng Yulin.

sentences.zh: 奏請主事唐景崧募健卒出關，與永福相犄角。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking Secretary Tang Jingsong to recruit stalwart soldiers and go beyond the passes, supporting Yongfu in mutual flanking.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Secretary Tang Jingsong recruit troops and advance beyond the frontier to coordinate with Liu Yongfu in a pincer.

sentences.zh: 朝旨因就加永福提督、景崧五品卿銜，炯、延旭亦皆已至巡撫，當前敵，被劾得罪去，並坐舉者。

translations.literal: An imperial order thereupon promoted Yongfu to provincial commander and gave Jingsong fifth-rank noble rank; Jiong and Yanxu, who had already reached the rank of governor, faced the enemy in front, were impeached and punished and removed, and those who had recommended them were punished as well.
translations.idiomatic: The court then made Liu Yongfu a provincial commander and gave Tang Jingsong fifth-rank noble rank; Tang Jiong and Xu Yanxu, already governors, were impeached after failures at the front and removed, and those who had recommended them were punished too.

sentences.zh: 之洞獨以籌餉械勞，免議。

translations.literal: Zhidong alone, on account of labor in raising funds and ordnance, was exempted from censure.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidong alone escaped censure on the grounds of his work supplying funds and arms.

sentences.zh: 廣西軍既敗於越，朝旨免鼎新，以提督蘇元春統其軍，而之洞復奏遣提督馮子材、總兵王孝祺等，皆宿將，於是滇、越兩軍合扼鎮南關，殊死戰，遂克諒山。

translations.literal: After the Guangxi army was defeated in Vietnam, an imperial order removed Dingxin and put provincial commander Su Yuanchun in command of his army; Zhidong again memorialized to dispatch provincial commander Feng Zicai, regional commander Wang Xiaoqi, and others, all veteran generals; thereupon the Yunnan and Vietnam armies united to hold Zhennanguan, fought a desperate battle, and took Lang Son.
translations.idiomatic: After the Guangxi army's defeat in Vietnam, Pan Dingxin was removed and Provincial Commander Su Yuanchun took over; Zhidong then sent veteran commanders Feng Zicai and Wang Xiaoqi; Yunnan and Guangxi forces united at Zhennanguan, fought a desperate battle, and captured Lang Son.

sentences.zh: 會法提督孤拔攻閩、浙，砲毀其坐船，孤拔殪，而我軍不知，法原停戰，廷議許焉。

translations.literal: It happened that French Admiral Courbet attacked Fujian and Zhejiang; cannon destroyed his flagship and Courbet perished, but our army did not know; France had originally proposed a ceasefire, and court deliberation approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile French Admiral Courbet attacked Fujian and Zhejiang; cannon fire destroyed his flagship and killed him, but Chinese forces did not know; France had already sought a truce, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 授李鴻章全權大臣，定約，以北圻為界。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang was appointed plenipotentiary to conclude a treaty setting the northern provinces of Vietnam as the boundary.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang was made plenipotentiary and concluded a treaty with Tonkin as the boundary.

sentences.zh: 敘克諒山功，賞花翎。

translations.literal: Recording the merit of taking Lang Son, he was granted peacock feathers.
translations.idiomatic: For the capture of Lang Son he was awarded peacock feathers.

sentences.zh: 之洞恥言和，則陰自圖強，設廣東水陸師學堂，創槍砲廠，開礦務局。

translations.literal: Zhidong was ashamed of talk of peace and secretly sought self-strengthening: he established Guangdong naval and military academies, founded an arsenal, and opened a mining bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed of the peace settlement, Zhidong quietly pursued self-strengthening: he founded Guangdong naval and military schools, an arsenal, and a mining bureau.

sentences.zh: 疏請大治水師，歲提專款購兵艦。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking to develop the navy on a large scale and set aside annual special funds to purchase warships.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized for a major naval buildup and annual dedicated funds to buy warships.

sentences.zh: 復立廣雅書院。

translations.literal: He also founded the Guangya Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He also established the Guangya Academy.

sentences.zh: 武備文事並舉。

translations.literal: Military preparedness and literary affairs were pursued together.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued both military training and literary education together.

sentences.zh: 十二年，兼署巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he concurrently served as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he also served as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 於兩粵邊防控制之宜，輒多更置。

translations.literal: As to what was fitting for controlling the frontier defenses of the two Guang provinces, he often made many changes in deployment.
translations.idiomatic: He frequently reorganized frontier defenses in the two Guang provinces.

sentences.zh: 著沿海險要圖說上之。

translations.literal: He composed and presented an illustrated account of coastal strategic points.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled an illustrated report on coastal defenses and submitted it to the court.

sentences.zh: 在粵六年，調補兩湖。

translations.literal: After six years in Guangdong he was transferred to fill the post in the two Hu provinces.
translations.idiomatic: After six years in Guangdong he was transferred to the two Hu provinces.

sentences.zh: 會海軍衙門奏請修京通鐵路，臺諫爭陳鐵路之害，請停辦。

translations.literal: When the Naval Office memorialized to build the Beijing-Tongzhou Railway, censors and remonstrators disputed, stating the harm of railways and asking that construction be halted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Naval Office proposed building the Beijing-Tongzhou railway, censors protested its dangers and demanded that work stop.

sentences.zh: 翁同龢等請試修邊地，便用兵；

translations.literal: Weng Tonghe and others asked to try building in frontier regions for convenience in using troops;
translations.idiomatic: Weng Tonghe and others proposed trial lines in frontier regions to facilitate troop movement;

sentences.zh: 徐會灃請改修德州濟寧路，利漕運。

translations.literal: Xu Huifeng asked to change construction to the Dezhou-Jining route to benefit grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huifeng urged building the Dezhou-Jining line instead to aid the grain transport system.

sentences.zh: 之洞議曰：「修路之利，以通土貨、厚民生為最大，徵兵、轉餉次之。

translations.literal: Zhidong argued, saying: "The benefit of building railways is greatest in moving local goods and enriching people's livelihood; raising troops and transporting provisions come next.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidong argued: "The greatest benefit of railways is moving local goods and enriching the people; military transport comes second.

sentences.zh: 今宜自京外盧溝橋起，經河南以達湖北漢口鎮。

translations.literal: Now it is fitting to start from Lugou Bridge outside the capital, pass through Henan, and reach Hankou in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: The line should run from Lugou Bridge outside Beijing through Henan to Hankou in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 此幹路樞紐，中國大利所萃也。

translations.literal: This trunk route is the pivot where China's great benefits converge.
translations.idiomatic: This trunk line would be the pivot on which China's greatest advantages would turn.

sentences.zh: 河北路成，則三晉之轍接於井陘，關隴之驂交於洛口；

translations.literal: When the Hebei section is complete, the wheel tracks of the three Jin regions will connect at Jingxing, and the paired horses of Guanlong will meet at Luokou;
translations.idiomatic: Once the Hebei section was built, Shanxi would link at Jingxing and Shaanxi and Gansu at Luokou;

sentences.zh: 自河以南，則東引淮、吳，南通湘、蜀，萬里聲息，刻期可通。

translations.literal: south of the river, it would draw eastward to Huai and Wu, southward connect Hunan and Sichuan; news and traffic ten thousand li apart could reach each other within set periods.
translations.idiomatic: south of the Yellow River it would reach east to the Huai and Wu regions and south to Hunan and Sichuan, so that news and goods could cross thousands of li within fixed time.

sentences.zh: 其便利有數端：內處腹地，無慮引敵，利一；

translations.literal: Its conveniences have several points: lying within the interior, no worry of drawing in the enemy—benefit one;
translations.idiomatic: He listed seven advantages: running through the interior, it would not invite enemy invasion—first;

sentences.zh: 原野廣漠，墳廬易避，利二；

translations.literal: the open wilderness makes graves and dwellings easy to avoid—benefit two;
translations.idiomatic: the open countryside would make graves and dwellings easy to avoid—second;

sentences.zh: 廠盛站多，役夫賈客可舍舊圖新，利三；

translations.literal: many factories and stations allow laborers and merchants to abandon old ways for new—benefit three;
translations.idiomatic: numerous workshops and stations would let laborers and merchants shift to new livelihoods—third;

sentences.zh: 以一路控八九省之衢，人貨輻輳，足裕餉源，利四；

translations.literal: one route controls the thoroughfares of eight or nine provinces; people and goods converge, sufficient to enrich revenue sources—benefit four;
translations.idiomatic: one line would command the routes of eight or nine provinces, concentrating people and goods to enrich revenue—fourth;

sentences.zh: 近畿有事，淮、楚精兵崇朝可集，利五；

translations.literal: if trouble arises near the capital, elite Huai and Chu troops can assemble within a morning—benefit five;
translations.idiomatic: if trouble arose near the capital, elite Huai and Chu troops could assemble within a day—fifth;

sentences.zh: 太原旺煤鐵，運行便則開採必多，利六；

translations.literal: Taiyuan abounds in coal and iron; convenient transport will surely increase mining—benefit six;
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan's rich coal and iron would be mined far more once transport was easy—sixth;

sentences.zh: 海上用兵，漕運無梗，利七。

translations.literal: if war occurs at sea, grain transport by the Grand Canal will be unimpeded—benefit seven.
translations.idiomatic: in a war at sea, Grand Canal grain transport would remain unimpeded—seventh.

sentences.zh: 有此七利，分段分年成之。

translations.literal: With these seven benefits, it should be completed section by section and year by year.
translations.idiomatic: With these seven advantages, he proposed building the line in sections over successive years.

sentences.zh: 北路責之直隸總督，南路責之湖廣總督，副以河南巡撫。」

translations.literal: The northern section would be charged to the governor-general of Zhili, the southern to the governor-general of Huguang, with the governor of Henan assisting.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhili governor-general would oversee the northern section, the Huguang governor-general the southern, with the Henan governor assisting.

sentences.zh: 得旨報可，遂有移楚之命。

translations.literal: An imperial order approved the report, and thereupon came the order transferring him to Chu.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved, and he received orders to transfer to Huguang.

sentences.zh: 大冶產鐵，江西萍鄉產煤，之洞乃奏開鍊鐵廠漢陽大別山下，資路用，兼設槍砲鋼藥專廠。

translations.literal: Daye produced iron and Pingxiang in Jiangxi produced coal; Zhidong then memorialized to open an ironworks at the foot of Mount Dabie at Hanyang to supply the railway, and concurrently established specialized factories for guns, cannon, steel, and powder.
translations.idiomatic: With iron from Daye and coal from Pingxiang in Jiangxi, he founded an ironworks at Hanyang beneath Mount Dabie to supply the railway, along with specialized factories for firearms, artillery, steel, and powder.

sentences.zh: 又以荊襄宜桑棉麻枲而饒皮革，設織布、紡紗、繅絲、制麻革諸局，佐之以堤工，通之以幣政。

translations.literal: Because Jing-Xiang was suited to mulberry, cotton, hemp, and ramie and abounded in leather, he established bureaus for weaving cloth, spinning yarn, reeling silk, and making hemp and leather goods, assisted by dike works and linked by currency policy.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jing-Xiang region was suited to mulberry, cotton, hemp, and ramie and rich in leather, he set up textile, spinning, silk-reeling, and leather works, supported them with dike projects, and tied them to monetary policy.

sentences.zh: 由是湖北財賦稱饒，土木工作亦日興矣。

translations.literal: From this Hubei's revenues were said to be abundant, and construction work also flourished day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Hubei's revenues grew abundant, and construction boomed.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，中東事棘，代劉坤一督兩江，至則巡閱江防，購新出後膛砲，改築西式砲台，設專將專兵領之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, when the Sino-Japanese affair grew critical, he replaced Liu Kunyi as governor-general of the two Jiang regions; on arrival he inspected river defenses, purchased newly produced breech-loading cannon, rebuilt Western-style forts, and appointed dedicated generals and troops to command them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, when the Sino-Japanese crisis erupted, he replaced Liu Kunyi as governor-general of the two Jiangs; on arrival he inspected river defenses, bought new breech-loading guns, rebuilt Western-style forts, and assigned dedicated commanders and troops.

sentences.zh: 募德人教練，名曰「江南自強軍」。

translations.literal: He recruited Germans as instructors for a force called the "Jiangnan Self-Strengthening Army."
translations.idiomatic: He hired German instructors for a force called the "Jiangnan Self-Strengthening Army."

sentences.zh: 採東西規制，廣立武備、農工商、鐵路、方言、軍醫諸學堂。

translations.literal: Adopting Eastern and Western regulations, he broadly founded schools for military affairs, agriculture, industry, commerce, railways, foreign languages, and military medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Adopting Eastern and Western models, he founded schools for military affairs, agriculture, industry, commerce, railways, foreign languages, and military medicine.

sentences.zh: 尋還任湖北。

translations.literal: Soon he returned to his post in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: He soon returned to his post in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 時國威新挫，朝士日議變法，廢時文，改試策論。

translations.literal: At that time national prestige had just suffered defeat; court scholars daily discussed reform, abolishing the eight-legged essay and changing examinations to policy essays.
translations.idiomatic: National prestige had just been shaken; court officials daily debated reform, abolishing the eight-legged essay and shifting examinations to policy essays.

sentences.zh: 之洞言：「廢時文，非廢五經、四書也，故文體必正，命題之意必嚴。

translations.literal: Zhidong said: "Abolishing the timed essay is not abolishing the Five Classics and Four Books; therefore literary form must be correct and the intent of examination topics must be strict.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidong said: "Abolishing the examination essay is not abolishing the Five Classics and Four Books; the literary form must remain correct and examination topics must be set with strict intent.

sentences.zh: 否則國家重教之旨不顯，必致不讀經文，背道忘本，非細故也。

translations.literal: Otherwise the state's emphasis on teaching will not be manifest, and it will surely lead to not reading the classics, turning from the Way and forgetting roots—this is no small matter.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the state's emphasis on classical learning will be lost, candidates will stop reading the classics, turn from the Way, and forget their roots—this is no small matter.

sentences.zh: 今宜首場試史論及本朝政法，二場試時務，三場以經義終焉。

translations.literal: Now the first session should test historical essays and current-dynasty government and law, the second current affairs, and the third end with classical interpretation.
translations.idiomatic: The first session should test historical essays and current government and law, the second current affairs, and the third classical interpretation.

sentences.zh: 各隨場去留而層遞取之，庶少流弊。」

translations.literal: Candidates should pass or fail at each session and be selected in layers, so that abuses may be somewhat reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates should pass or fail at each session in sequence, which would reduce abuses.

sentences.zh: 又言：「武科宜罷騎射、刀石，專試火器。

translations.literal: He also said: "The military examination should abandon mounted archery and stone-lifting and test firearms exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that the military examinations drop mounted archery and strength tests and test firearms exclusively.

sentences.zh: 欲挽重文輕武之習，必使兵皆識字，勵行伍以科舉。」

translations.literal: To reverse the habit of honoring literature and slighting arms, soldiers must all be literate and the ranks encouraged through the civil service examinations.
translations.idiomatic: To reverse the habit of honoring scholars and slighting soldiers, troops must be literate and the ranks encouraged through the examination system.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，政變作，之洞先著勸學篇以見意，得免議。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year the political coup occurred; Zhidong had earlier written Exhortation to Learning to express his views and escaped censure.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, when the political coup occurred, Zhidong had already published his Exhortation to Learning to state his position and escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，京師拳亂，時坤一督兩江，鴻章督兩廣，袁世凱撫山東，要請之洞，同與外國領事定保護東南之約。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the Boxer disorder broke out in the capital; at that time Kunyi governed the two Jiangs, Hongzhang the two Guang, Yuan Shikai governed Shandong; they urgently invited Zhidong to join with foreign consuls in fixing an agreement to protect the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, when the Boxer uprising convulsed Beijing, Kunyi governed the two Jiangs, Li Hongzhang the two Guang, and Yuan Shikai Shandong; they urgently asked Zhidong to join foreign consuls in the agreement to protect the southeast.

sentences.zh: 及聯軍內犯，兩宮西幸，而東南幸無事。

translations.literal: When the allied armies invaded inland, the two palaces fled west, yet the southeast fortunately remained undisturbed.
translations.idiomatic: When the allied armies advanced inland and the court fled west, the southeast fortunately remained at peace.

sentences.zh: 明年，和議成，兩宮回鑾。

translations.literal: The next year peace was concluded and the two palaces returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The following year peace was concluded and the court returned to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 論功，加太子少保。

translations.literal: Recording merit, he was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: For his services he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 以兵事粗定，乃與坤一合上變法三疏。

translations.literal: As military affairs were roughly settled, he and Kunyi jointly submitted three memorials on reform.
translations.idiomatic: Once military affairs had settled somewhat, he and Liu Kunyi jointly submitted three reform memorials.

sentences.zh: 其論中國積弱不振之故，宜變通者十二事，宜採西法者十一事。

translations.literal: They discussed the reasons for China's long weakness and lack of recovery: twelve matters that should be changed, and eleven Western methods that should be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: They analyzed why China had remained weak, listing twelve areas for institutional change and eleven Western practices to adopt.

sentences.zh: 於是停捐納，去書吏，考差役，卹刑獄，籌八旗生計，裁屯衛，汰綠營，定礦律、商律、路律、交涉律，行銀圓，取印花稅，擴郵政。

translations.literal: Thereupon purchase of office was halted, clerks removed, runners examined, prisons treated with compassion, Eight Banner livelihood planned, military colonies cut, Green Standard troops reduced, mining, commercial, railway, and foreign-relations laws fixed, silver dollars circulated, stamp tax levied, and postal service expanded.
translations.idiomatic: Purchase of office was halted, clerks removed, runners examined, prisons reformed, Eight Banner livelihood addressed, military colonies cut, Green Standard troops reduced, mining, commercial, railway, and foreign-relations laws drafted, silver dollars introduced, stamp duties levied, and the postal service expanded.

sentences.zh: 其尤要者，則設學堂，停科舉，獎遊學。

translations.literal: Most important of all were establishing schools, halting the civil service examinations, and rewarding study abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Most important were establishing schools, ending the civil examinations, and rewarding study abroad.

sentences.zh: 皆次第行焉。

translations.literal: All were carried out in turn.
translations.idiomatic: These measures were enacted in turn.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，充督辦商務大臣，再署兩江總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he served as supervising minister of commerce and again acted as governor-general of the two Jiangs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he became supervising minister of commerce and again served as acting governor-general of the two Jiangs.

sentences.zh: 有道員私獻商人金二十萬為壽，請開礦海州，立劾罷之。

translations.literal: A circuit intendant privately presented a merchant two hundred thousand taels as a birthday gift and asked to open mines at Haizhou; Zhidong immediately impeached and removed him.
translations.idiomatic: When a circuit intendant privately accepted two hundred thousand taels from a merchant as a birthday gift in exchange for mining rights at Haizhou, Zhidong impeached and dismissed him at once.

sentences.zh: 考鹽法利弊，設兵輪緝私，歲有贏課。

translations.literal: He examined the advantages and disadvantages of the salt monopoly, established armed steamers to suppress smuggling, and each year had surplus revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He reviewed the salt monopoly, deployed armed steamers against smuggling, and produced annual surpluses.

sentences.zh: 明年，入覲，充經濟特科閱卷大臣，釐定大學堂章程，畢，仍命還任。

translations.literal: The next year he entered for audience, served as examiner for the special economic examination, settled the regulations of the university, and when finished was still ordered to return to his post.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he went to court, served as chief examiner for the special economic examination, finalized university regulations, and was then ordered back to his post.

sentences.zh: 陛辭奏對，請化除滿、漢畛域，以彰聖德，遏亂萌，上為動​​容。

translations.literal: At his farewell audience he memorialized asking to dissolve Manchu-Han barriers to manifest sagely virtue and check the sprouting of disorder; the emperor was moved.
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience he urged breaking down Manchu-Han barriers to manifest imperial virtue and forestall disorder; the emperor was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 旋裁巡撫，以之洞兼之。

translations.literal: Soon the governorship was abolished and Zhidong held it concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: The governorship was soon abolished and Zhidong held it concurrently.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，晉協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he was promoted to Associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year he was promoted to Associate Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 未幾，內召，擢體仁閣大學士，授軍機大臣，兼筦學部。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned to the capital, promoted to Grand Secretary of the Tiren Hall, appointed Grand Councilor, and concurrently put in charge of the Ministry of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to the capital, made Grand Secretary of the Tiren Hall, appointed to the Grand Council, and put in charge of the Ministry of Education.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，督辦粵漢鐵路。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he supervised the Canton-Hankou Railway.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year he supervised construction of the Canton-Hankou Railway.

sentences.zh: 德宗暨慈禧皇太后相繼崩，醇親王載灃監國攝政。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong and Empress Dowager Cixi died in succession; Prince Chun Zai Feng acted as regent for the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangxu and Empress Dowager Cixi died in succession, and Prince Chun Zai Feng became regent.

sentences.zh: 之洞以顧命重臣晉太子太保。

translations.literal: Zhidong, as a heavy minister entrusted at the deathbed, was advanced to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: As a deathbed entrusted minister, Zhidong was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 逾年，親貴浸用事，通私謁。

translations.literal: After a year, imperial kinsmen gradually wielded power and received private audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year imperial princes increasingly wielded power and accepted private audiences.

sentences.zh: 議立海軍，之洞言海軍費絀可緩立，爭之不得。

translations.literal: When a navy was discussed, Zhidong said naval funds were insufficient and establishment could be delayed; he contended but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: When a new navy was proposed, Zhidong argued that funds were insufficient and the project could wait, but he could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 移疾，遂卒，年七十三，朝野震悼。

translations.literal: He reported illness, then died, aged seventy-three; court and populace were shaken with grief.
translations.idiomatic: He reported illness and died at seventy-three; court and country mourned deeply.

sentences.zh: 贈太保，諡文襄。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Grand Tutor and honored with the posthumous title Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Tutor and given the posthumous title Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 之洞短身巨髯，風儀峻整。

translations.literal: Zhidong was short in stature with a great beard; his bearing was stern and dignified.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidong was short and heavily bearded, with a stern and dignified bearing.

sentences.zh: 蒞官所至，必有興作。

translations.literal: Wherever he took office there were always new undertakings.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served, he launched new projects.

sentences.zh: 務宏大，不問費多寡。

translations.literal: He pursued the grand and did not ask how great the expense.
translations.idiomatic: He thought on a grand scale and paid little heed to cost.

sentences.zh: 愛才好客，名流文士爭趨之。

translations.literal: He loved talent and received guests; eminent literary men vied to flock to him.
translations.idiomatic: He loved talent and entertained guests generously; leading scholars flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 任疆寄數十年，及卒，家不增一畝雲。

translations.literal: He held frontier responsibilities for several decades, and when he died his family had not increased by a single mu of land, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Though he held provincial power for decades, it is said that when he died his family had not gained a single extra mu of land.

sentences.zh: 瞿鴻禨，字子玖，湖南善化人。

translations.literal: Qu Hongji, courtesy name Zijiu, was a native of Shanhua in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Hongji, whose courtesy name was Zijiu, came from Shanhua in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 同治十年進士，授編修。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the tenth year of Tongzhi, he was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the tenth year of Tongzhi and was appointed a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，大考一等，擢侍講學士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu, in the great examination he placed first class and was promoted to attendant academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangxu he ranked first class in the palace examination and was promoted to attendant academician.

sentences.zh: 久乃遷詹事，晉內閣學士。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to tutor of the heir apparent and advanced to inner court academician.
translations.idiomatic: Only after a long interval was he made tutor to the heir apparent and then inner court academician.

sentences.zh: 先後典福建、廣西鄉試，督河南、浙江、四川學政。

translations.literal: He successively presided over the provincial examinations of Fujian and Guangxi and served as educational commissioner of Henan, Zhejiang, and Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over the provincial examinations in Fujian and Guangxi in turn and served as educational commissioner in Henan, Zhejiang, and Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 所行皆本功令，律下尤嚴。

translations.literal: All his measures followed official regulations, and discipline under his rule was especially strict.
translations.idiomatic: His administration strictly followed official regulations, and discipline under him was especially severe.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮戰事起，我師出平壤。

translations.literal: When the Korean war arose, our army advanced to Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out in Korea, Chinese forces advanced on Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 鴻禨上四路進兵之策，請兼募沿海漁人蜑戶編為舟師，使敵備多力分，庶可制勝。

translations.literal: Hongji submitted a plan for advancing by four routes and asked also to recruit coastal fishermen and Tanka boat people as a naval force, so that the enemy's preparations would be many and strength divided, and victory might thereby be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Hongji proposed a four-route advance and urged recruiting coastal fishermen and Tanka boat people into a naval force, arguing that dividing the enemy's attention would make victory possible.

sentences.zh: 及和議成，鴻禨方自蜀還，復奏言秦中地形險要，請豫建陪都。

translations.literal: When peace was concluded, Hongji had just returned from Sichuan and again memorialized that the terrain of Qin was strategically vital, asking to prepare in advance a secondary capital.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was concluded, Hongji had just returned from Sichuan and memorialized that the Qin region's terrain was strategically vital, urging the court to establish a secondary capital in advance.

sentences.zh: 日本增兵遼東，鴻禨以敵情叵測，請敕劉坤一、王文韶簡練勁旅，不可專任淮軍。

translations.literal: Japan increased troops in Liaodong; Hongji, because the enemy's intentions were hard to fathom, asked that Liu Kunyi and Wang Wenshao be ordered to select crack troops and that the Huai army alone not be relied on.
translations.idiomatic: When Japan reinforced its troops in Liaodong, Hongji, finding the enemy's intentions unpredictable, urged that Liu Kunyi and Wang Wenshao train crack forces and that the court not rely solely on the Huai army.

sentences.zh: 適坤一奏劾山西將賀星明侵餉，革職，鴻禨言：「刑賞治天下之大柄，軍紀廢弛已久，宜嚴懲以儆其餘。」

translations.literal: It happened that Kunyi memorialized impeaching Shanxi general He Xingming for embezzling pay and had him dismissed from office; Hongji said: "Punishment and reward are the great handles by which the realm is governed; military discipline has long been lax and should be sternly punished to warn the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Liu Kunyi impeached Shanxi General He Xingming for embezzling pay and had him dismissed; Hongji argued: "Reward and punishment are the great levers of government; military discipline has long been lax, and stern punishment is needed to warn others.

sentences.zh: 又：「葉志超、龔照嶼等敗軍辱國，罪當死。

translations.literal: He also said: "Ye Zhichao, Gong Zhaoyu, and others disgraced the nation by defeat; their crime deserves death.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Ye Zhichao, Gong Zhaoyu, and others shamed the nation in defeat and deserve death.

sentences.zh: 和約既定，勢不能與勾，宜籍其財產，或令巨款捐贖，然後貸其一死。」

translations.literal: Now that the treaty is fixed, it is impossible to deal with them in the usual way; their property should be confiscated, or they should be made to pay a huge sum in ransom, and only then spare their lives.
translations.idiomatic: With the treaty already signed they cannot be executed in the usual way; their property should be confiscated, or they should pay a huge ransom, and only then be spared.

sentences.zh: 皆不報。

translations.literal: None received response.
translations.idiomatic: None of these proposals was adopted.

sentences.zh: 旋遷禮部侍郎，出督江蘇學政。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to vice minister of Rites and went out to supervise education in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made vice minister of Rites and appointed educational commissioner of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 請罷武科。

translations.literal: He asked to abolish the military examination.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to abolish the military examinations.

sentences.zh: 兩宮西狩，鴻禨差竣詣行在，道授左都御使，晉工部尚書，仍以西安陪都為言。

translations.literal: When the two palaces fled west, Hongji, his term of duty completed, proceeded to the traveling court; en route he was appointed Left Censor-in-Chief and promoted to Minister of Works, again speaking of Xi'an as a secondary capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the court fled west, Hongji finished his assignment and hurried to the traveling court; en route he was made Left Censor-in-Chief and Minister of Works, again urging Xi'an as a secondary capital.

sentences.zh: 既至，命直軍機，兼充政務處大臣。

translations.literal: When he arrived, he was ordered to attend the Grand Council and concurrently serve as minister of the Bureau of Government Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he joined the Grand Council and also served on the Bureau of Government Affairs.

sentences.zh: 請以策論試士，開經濟特科，汰書吏，悉允行。

translations.literal: He asked to test scholars with policy essays, open a special economic examination, and reduce clerks; all were approved and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed policy-essay examinations, a special economic examination, and reduction of clerks; all were approved.

sentences.zh: 改總理各國事務衙門為外務部，班六部上，以鴻禨為尚書。

translations.literal: The Zongli Yamen for all nations' affairs was changed to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, ranked above the Six Ministries, with Hongji as minister.
translations.idiomatic: The Zongli Yamen was reorganized as the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, ranked above the Six Ministries, with Hongji as its minister.

sentences.zh: 時方與各國議和，鴻禨治事明敏，諳究外交，承旨擬諭，語中竅要，頗當上意焉。

translations.literal: At that time peace was being negotiated with the various powers; Hongji handled affairs with keen clarity, was well versed in foreign relations, drafted edicts on imperial orders, hit the vital points in language, and greatly suited the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: While peace was being negotiated with the powers, Hongji handled affairs with sharp efficiency, knew foreign affairs thoroughly, drafted edicts that hit the essential points, and greatly pleased the throne.

sentences.zh: 扈蹕回鑾，賞黃馬褂，加太子太保。

translations.literal: Escorting the return to the capital, he was granted the yellow jacket and given the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On the court's return to Beijing he received the yellow jacket and was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 自新政議起，興學、通商、勸工諸政，有司多藉端巧取。

translations.literal: From the time the new policies were debated, in measures to promote schools, commerce, and industry, local officials often used pretexts to exact clever levies.
translations.idiomatic: Once the new policies were debated, local officials often used school, commerce, and industry programs as pretexts for extortion.

sentences.zh: 鴻禨請降旨禁革苛派，任民間自辦。

translations.literal: Hongji asked that an edict be issued forbidding harsh exactions and allowing the people to manage affairs themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Hongji asked for an edict forbidding harsh levies and allowing local initiatives.

sentences.zh: 又請旨以戶部正雜諸款供地方正用，宮中歲費，遵先朝定例，量入為出，不便自戶部增撥。

translations.literal: He also asked that regular and miscellaneous funds of the Ministry of Revenue supply local regular expenses, that the palace annual expenditure follow the fixed precedents of former reigns, measuring outgo by income, and that it not be convenient to increase allocations from the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that regular and miscellaneous revenue fund local needs, that palace expenses follow former precedents and live within means, and that the Ministry of Revenue not be asked for extra allocations.

sentences.zh: 裁汰內務府冗員，用節糜費。

translations.literal: Redundant personnel of the Imperial Household Department were cut to save wasteful expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: He cut redundant staff in the Imperial Household Department to curb waste.

sentences.zh: 充中日議約全權大臣。

translations.literal: He served as plenipotentiary for the Sino-Japanese treaty negotiations.
translations.idiomatic: He served as plenipotentiary in the Sino-Japanese treaty negotiations.

sentences.zh: 是時中外咸以立憲為請，朝廷下詔豫備憲政始基，勗天下以忠君尊孔、尚公尚武尚實，用鴻禨言也。

translations.literal: At that time inside and outside the court all requested constitutional government; the court issued an edict preparing the foundation of constitutional government, exhorting the realm to loyalty to the ruler, reverence for Confucius, esteem for public spirit, martial spirit, and practicality—Hongji's words were used.
translations.idiomatic: When court and country alike called for constitutional government, the throne issued an edict laying the groundwork for constitutional reform, exhorting loyalty to the ruler, reverence for Confucius, and esteem for public spirit, martial virtue, and practical learning—language drawn from Hongji's proposals.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he became Associate Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year he was made Associate Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 特旨派議改官制大臣，鴻禨以樞廷事冗辭。

translations.literal: By special edict he was appointed a minister to deliberate on reform of the official system; Hongji declined on the grounds that Grand Council business was too burdensome.
translations.idiomatic: By special edict he was appointed to deliberate on bureaucratic reform, but Hongji declined, citing the press of Grand Council business.

sentences.zh: 旋命與大學士孫家鼐复核，頗有裁正焉。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to review the matter jointly with Grand Secretary Sun Jianai, and made many corrections.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to review the proposals with Grand Secretary Sun Jianai and made many corrections.

sentences.zh: 鴻禨持躬清刻，以儒臣驟登政地，銳於任事。

translations.literal: Hongji conducted himself with austere integrity; as a Confucian scholar suddenly elevated to political power, he was keen in undertaking affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hongji lived with austere integrity; as a scholar suddenly thrust into high office, he was eager to act.

sentences.zh: 素善岑春煊，春煊入朝，留長郵傳部。

translations.literal: He had long been on good terms with Cen Chunxuan; when Chunxuan entered court, he was kept to head the Ministry of Posts and Communications.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been close to Cen Chunxuan, who on entering court was kept on to head the Ministry of Posts and Communications.

sentences.zh: 密疏劾慶親王奕劻，奕劻惡春煊，遂及鴻禨。

translations.literal: In a secret memorial he impeached Prince Qing Yikuang; Yikuang hated Chunxuan, and Hongji was implicated as well.
translations.idiomatic: In a secret memorial he impeached Prince Qing Yikuang; Yikuang hated Cen Chunxuan, and Hongji was drawn into the feud.

sentences.zh: 會鴻禨因直言忤太后旨，侍講學士惲毓鼎劾以攬權恣縱，遂罷斥歸里。

translations.literal: It happened that Hongji, because blunt speech offended the empress dowager's will, was impeached by attendant academician Yun Yuding for monopolizing power and acting willfully, and was dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongji's blunt remonstrance offended the empress dowager, Attendant Academician Yun Yuding impeached him for arrogating power, and he was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，湘變起，流寓上海，旋卒。

translations.literal: In the xinhai year rebellion broke out in Hunan; he lived in exile in Shanghai and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: In 1911, when rebellion broke out in Hunan, he took refuge in Shanghai and soon died.

sentences.zh: 後追諡文慎。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously honored with the title Wenshen.
translations.idiomatic: He was later given the posthumous title Wenshen.

sentences.zh: 論曰：德宗親政，憤於外侮，思變法自強。

translations.literal: The commentary says: When Emperor Dezong personally took power, indignant at foreign insult, he thought to reform the laws and strengthen himself.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: When Emperor Guangxu took personal rule, angry at foreign encroachment, he sought reform and self-strengthening.

sentences.zh: 乃以輔導無人，戊戌黨禍，庚子匪亂，遂相繼而作。

translations.literal: Yet because there was no one to guide him, the party disaster of the wuxu year and the bandit disorder of the gengzi year followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: But lacking able counselors, the disaster of 1898 and the Boxer uprising of 1900 followed in turn.

sentences.zh: 太后再出垂簾，初堅復舊，繼勉圖新。

translations.literal: The empress dowager again came forth behind the curtain; at first she firmly sought restoration of the old, then strove to pursue the new.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager resumed regency, she first insisted on restoring the old order, then pressed on toward reform.

sentences.zh: 宣統改元，議行憲政。

translations.literal: When the Xuantong reign began, constitutional government was debated and enacted.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Xuantong reign, constitutional government was debated and undertaken.

sentences.zh: 政體既變，國本遂搖，而大勢不可問矣。

translations.literal: Once the political system changed, the foundation of the state was shaken, and the great trend could no longer be questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Once the political system changed, the foundations of the state shook, and the larger course of events was beyond remedy.

sentences.zh: 榮祿屢參大變，文韶久達世務。

translations.literal: Rong Lu repeatedly took part in great upheavals; Wenshao long understood affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Rong Lu took part repeatedly in great crises; Wenshao had long mastered affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 鴻禨後起，參議立憲，終以失寵太后，不免放斥。

translations.literal: Hongji rose later, took part in deliberating constitutional government, but in the end lost favor with the empress dowager and could not escape dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Hongji rose later and helped debate constitutional government, but ultimately lost the empress dowager's favor and was cast out.

sentences.zh: 唯之洞一時稱賢，而監國攝政，親貴用事，欲挽救而未能，遂以憂死。

translations.literal: Only Zhidong was for a time called worthy; yet under regency rule, imperial kinsmen wielded power; he wished to rescue affairs but could not, and thus died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zhang Zhidong was for a time hailed as a worthy minister; yet under the regency, imperial princes held power, and though he tried to save the situation he could not, and died in distress.

sentences.zh: 人之雲亡，邦國殄瘁，尚何言哉？

translations.literal: When men depart like clouds, the state is wasted and afflicted—what more can be said?
translations.idiomatic: When worthy men pass like clouds, the state is laid waste—what more is there to say?
